page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results place the instance's CPU and memory performance primarily in the average tier. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 7393.32 and the PassMark CPU score of 8349.76 represent middle-tier capabilities. Memory bandwidth is also moderate, with read-only large block speeds at 52.02 GB/sec and write speeds at 40.05 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%, indicating potential limitations under highly parallelized compute-heavy workloads.

Given the 64.0 GB memory capacity paired with moderate CPU performance, this instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extreme parallel processing power. Appropriate workloads include database operations, caching layers, and text processing. It is less suitable for intensive machine learning tasks, as demonstrated by its poor prompt processing speed of 10.36 tokens/sec on medium LLM models and its lack of GPU acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, this instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 8349.76 and a static web serving throughput of 7.05 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded performance is relatively weak, as shown by its Geekbench multi-core score of 4476.0. This resource profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy but compute-moderate tasks. It is best suited for database operations, caching, and text processing, while being less optimal for parallelized compute-intensive tasks or large-scale machine learning inference.
